blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A method creates a small Point that never leaves the method, and the method becomes hot. What can HotSpot's C2 compiler do with that allocation?

options.text: Place the whole Point object in the method's stack frame instead of the heap.
options.says: HotSpot does not allocate whole objects on the stack; the page says so explicitly.

options.text: Remove the allocation and keep the Point's fields as plain local values.
options.says: That is scalar replacement: escape analysis proves the object does not escape, so its fields become locals in registers or stack slots and no heap allocation happens.

options.text: Nothing, since every object must be allocated on the heap and collected later.
options.says: Escape analysis is the exception the page names: a non-escaping allocation can be eliminated entirely.

questions.stem: A cache should keep its entries until the heap is nearly full, and give them up then. Which reference should hold each entry?

options.text: A WeakReference, cleared by the collector once no strong reference remains.
options.says: A weak reference is cleared by the first GC cycle that finds the object only weakly reachable, even when memory is plentiful.

options.text: A PhantomReference, enqueued by the collector once the entry has been finalized.
options.says: A phantom reference's get() always returns null, so a cache could never read its entry back; it is for post-mortem cleanup.

options.text: A SoftReference, cleared by the collector when it comes under memory pressure.
options.says: Soft references are cleared only under memory pressure, and all of them before an OutOfMemoryError, which is exactly a memory-sensitive cache's need.

concepts: HotSpot never allocates a whole object on the stack; escape analysis can instead remove a non-escaping allocation by scalar replacement.
Soft references are cleared only under memory pressure, weak references by the first collection that finds them weakly reachable, and a phantom reference's get() is always null.
